**What already meets the bar.** The clamor and the solo era (17),
the scouting board with the schools and the market (17), the red
weeks and the last statement (16), the debut (15), the office door
and the friction stream (15), the landing and the music-show weeks
(14). These are the loops the last two years built on purpose and
they read like it — a board or a file the player returns to, doors
during the run, memory afterwards. The spotlight's 8 is partly by
design ("presence, not power", §88): its reads and flavor are the
best in the game and it was never meant to decide anything; its gap
is that the sightings never accumulate.

### What the four slices agree on

**1. Arc and teeth are deep; the event is thin.** The §91 comeback
work pays and remembers almost everywhere (Arc 3, Teeth 3 on the
landing, the shows, the debut) and rarely happens to the player as a
night. The release is one tick: twelve letters arrive at once and
the one that says it landed is `high`, not critical, so a loud week
can trim it (sim.js:160). The era has no end: `promoUntil` passes
and nothing in the engine reads its passing — no last stage, no
tally, no letter (every reader of promoUntil is a guard). The
repackage is one button whose own announcement the engine composes
and the UI throws away (debut.js:393 returns the note; app.js:1163
toasts its own line), with no choice inside it and no mark in the
discography (`repackageOf` is rendered nowhere). The pressing's card
promises a memo ("overpress and the warehouse writes the memo",
views_studio.js:469) that was trimmed in §89 and never came back —
`overpress` is computed, archived and shown nowhere. The commission
is four picks, two silent weeks and a chip; the pitch is a card list
that refreshes without a letter. The same shape on the road: the
tour is four knobs, then two to eight weeks of near-identical
normal-priority leg letters (only the airport is critical,
tour.js:279), then a one-line count; the engine rates every night
(stage.js:264-268 sells the next week on it) and none of it reaches
a door, a Today card or the calendar strip (sim.js's upcoming lists
no legs); the encore is automatic (tour.js:172-174). Festival season
is the most frequent scene in the game and the thinnest per
occurrence: one invite body, one sentence per night, and the booked
slot vanishes from every page until it plays. The Japan weeks are a
button, a fade to black and a letter.

**2. The people's lifespans have doors at the forks and nothing
between.** The trainee years: two dials, four silent weeks, an
evaluation sheet written at `flavor` priority (rituals.js:112,124)
— the trainee's only ceremony is the first letter the week trims —
and the three-year trainee paper is rendered nowhere (no `js/ui`
reader of `traineeContract`). The list on the wall, the most
repeated ceremony of a career, is a modal of the exec's sentences
(app.js:1116-1130) with no letter for the room and no door for the
ace left off. The absences are the purest plan → wait → result loops
left: a two-year service chapter is a chip and a date, "the desk has
no verbs here; nobody does", and both unanswered service doors file
their default at no cost (military.js:228-235, 266-271). How a group
ends is a status flip with a good sentence on it: the farewell lap
is announced ("the staff have started filming everything",
contracts.js:306-307) and nothing reads `contract.leaving` for two
years; the last contract's expiry is one `high` letter; the archive
card reads "0 members" for an act that ended by expiry because
`finalLineup` is written only by disbandGroup (group.js:347;
views_groups.js:44-48); a departed idol's file "stays open forever"
and is reachable from no list; no rival ever signs her and no "she
debuted elsewhere" letter exists.

**3. Characters without faces.** Six executives share one voice: the
`personality` field on every exec (data.js) is read by no engine
module, the exec has no card, tenure is never shown, and trust at
"gone" costs nothing (the firing §86 E3 deferred). The funds are a
hash-picked letterhead per week, so no fund remembers you. The
rivals have a philosophy word and a scoreboard, no head, no voice,
no door, and no memory of what you did to them — `founderGrudge` is
an exemption flag, never behaviour. The national chart's titans have
no page and never crowd your week (`crowdPenalty` counts rival
releases only, industry.js:340-343). The press is a voice without an
outlet. The staff are hired as people through the best-composed scene
in the company slice and then kept as multipliers: no review, no
credit, no leaving on their own terms (nothing in hires.js retires or
resigns a chair; the bot never releases one). The board, unless
founded, has no names; the founder's three speak twice per career.
The fandom has fourteen named regulars and keeps receipts, and its
only event is the truck.

**4. Silence is often the safe answer.** The house law is that
silence has teeth, and most of the game honours it (the door, the
friction stream, the table, the red weeks). The exceptions, every one
verified: the red-ink scene expires free where both answers cost
(money.js:314-318); the diagnosis expires into full rest with no mark
on anyone (medical.js:107-117); the service plan and the papers
expire into their defaults at no cost; the offer's "leverage" is
budget and trust against decline's smaller trust with nothing
recorded — strictly dominant (risefall.js:338-346); the festival's
"send regrets" writes a ledger count while the letter says "the
organizers keep notes" (festivals.js:196-207); the distributor's
"stay" is a toast, and because nothing records the refusal the
courting call re-opens the next week with a high letter for as long
as the number holds (money.js:239-247); board season's "point at the
artists" does nothing (staff.js:128); the new chair's two answers
both reward (tenure.js:149-158); the promo offer's decline promises
"they wrote it down" while only cancellations write the broadcaster's
ledger (promo.js:243-246); the interview's pass is forgotten by the
market; the lightstick is a one-shot net gain with no trade-off
(constituency.js:168-169); the café notice and the fandom-name
choice are cosmetic; unpairing writers and defusing a rivalry are
silent; the met mandate is consumed with no letter (mandate.js:
88-102).

**5. Depth that exists and cannot be reached or read.** The engine
computes `KP.gravityWord` — the transcendence read in words, "one of
the room" to "bigger than the group?" — and no view renders it; the
clamor arrives as a chip after the feature. `renewalRead` bands the
table two years early and is never surfaced before the folder.
`p.evalHistory` keeps twelve ranks and the board shows the last.
`toursDone` and the tour's per-member stage counts are never
rendered; there is no tour record. `jpFans`, the rung ladder and the
partner are never a page. The distributor's tier, the fanclub's tier
and anniversary, the running quarter (`books.cur`), the exec's
tenure, `objectiveHistory`, `state.career`, `estate.folded`, the
first trophy's week, the road manager's name on a card — none has a
reader in `js/ui`. The choreographer's track record is "written and
never read" by its own module's admission (pipeline.js:222-226);
writer heat exists in the ledger and is shown nowhere. The returnRun
scene — the alum's return to the stage with her old group, the one
door that would make the solo era bittersweet — opens only for a solo
act with `originGroupId`, which only graduateToSolo writes, and
graduateToSolo has no UI and no bot call: a registered scene nobody
can reach. releaseSoloAlbum is bot-only.

**6. The one queue.** Every "she comes to you" scene — the five
frictions, the two door asks, the two gravity knocks, the scar, the
spotlight's call, the walkout — goes through one weekly pick
(knock.js:54-76; KNOCK gapWeeks 1, chance .6, personGapWeeks 6).
Whatever the roster, the player answers one person-question every
two or three weeks and a given person knocks at most every six. This
is a ruled cadence (§40), not a bug, and it is why a six-member room
with three live frictions still yields one question a fortnight and
why the quiet no — the stream's best scene — never reached the soak.
It is a lever for the owner's hand, named here because every
person-depth release below pours into the same funnel.

**7. The inbox law trims the game's own moments.** The law is right
(five a week, critical bypasses) and some of what it trims is the
climax: the landing letter at `high`; the evaluation sheet and the
Season's Greetings at `flavor`; the tour's leg letters at normal; the
catalog push's wind-down at `flavor`; and weeks 44–48 pile the
greetings, the nominations, board season, the gayo invitation, the
awards and the Q4 close against the same five slots. Two signposts
mislead: the landing says "Full report in the Studio" and the report
button lives on the group page (sim.js:162, views_groups.js:521); a
debut's first stage is labeled "THE COMEBACK STAGE" (shows.js:273).
One modal contradicts the engine: launching the in-house solo career
says "{She} leaves the lineup warmly" while the engine keeps her
seat (app.js:838 vs gravity.js:94).

**8. Flavor is the weakest column outside the record.** The §93
expansion gave the heavy inds families and left the scene bodies and
the money letters alone: eleven of fourteen company loops and nine of
twelve world loops are single templates where the season got
families — every saga letter, the offer, the fund's sheet, the
quarterly close (52 identical letters a career), the rungs of the red
ladder, the obituary, the festival night, the tour's three city
lines, the service's every letter ("the event the whole anticipation
system builds toward" has no family). A player who dies twice reads
the identical page.

**9. Three reveal-law slips.** "Since debut: Vocals +7 · Dance +3"
(views_talent.js:426-435) prints raw deltas of the hidden talent
scale — deliberate in §88 C ("the work, in numbers") and flagged by
two slices independently; a band word would keep the law. The solo
project's "cut numbers" print the composite score as digits (debut.
js:1258). Three letters print "Reception N" raw where the Career tab
uses the word (gravity.js:488-491, group.js:438, outside.js:262).
Borderline: the power ranking's score column (views_industry.js:
104-110) — the deltas and ranks carry the read alone.

### The shelf — agreed and unbuilt

Ruled or planned in earlier sittings, never scheduled, still true:
**the imprint** (§55.11, §39 slot 13 — the associate label, the
founding machinery in reverse, "next on approval" three ledger
entries running before the §80 consult overtook it); **the wardrobe
department** (§39 slot 14 — named stylists and choreographers with
chemistry, poachable; today stylists are flavor strings and the
eight choreographers cannot be chosen); **the player-owned academy**
(§84's own prequel, "the long answer" to the powers' head start);
**the offer's accept path** (running the imperial house, §73 S18 —
the succession machinery it needed exists); **the firing** (§86 E3 —
trust at "gone" has no consequence). Capacitor stays parked by
ruling.

### The recommendation

Ordered by how often a human lives the loop times how silent it is,
with the cheap wiring first because every release after it reads
better once the existing depth is reachable. Each is a full-ritual
release; shapes only, numbers measure-first; the bot learns every
verb; the owner reorders at will.

**1. The wiring (depth hygiene — one release, like the audit; SHIPPED v0.11.5, as-built below).** Make
what exists reachable and honest: render gravityWord, the renewal
forecast in words, evaluation trajectory, the trainee paper, the tour
record and `toursDone`, festival bookings on the strip and the group
page, the Japan ladder, the distributor and the fanclub on the books
card, the running quarter, the exec's tenure and the chapters; the
warehouse memo and a restock door; the repackage's note sent and
`repackageOf` in the discography; the landing letter critical and
first in its week; the evaluation sheet and the greetings on a
priority ladder; the signposts and the modal copy fixed; the free
answers given their cost (leverage recorded on the rival, regrets
remembered by the organizer, "stay" remembered by the distributor,
the red-ink and service expiries with a mark, the board's third
answer with a meaning, the interview's pass with a memory); the three
reveal slips banded; graduateToSolo given a door or returnRun
retired. Measured by the same soak; nothing about outcomes moves.

**2. The stages, lived (the tour and festival season; SHIPPED v0.11.7, §98).** The season's
shape on its nearest cousin. An "On the road" Today card like "On the
air": the next city named before it plays, the room against demand in
words, last night's band. Doors during the road: the encore offer at
a sold-out stop (second night / rest the room / move on — today the
encore is automatic), the road presser after a fumbled night
(statement / ride, the edit's shape), the setlist swap when the
fandom's b-side pick is loud. A weekly moment family (the crowd sang
her lines, the ment that went long, the sign in two languages, the
rain set) through `momentOf`'s pattern. The wrap read city by city as
a ceremony — the night that went wrong and the one that went right —
and a tour record on the group page. Festivals on the same machinery:
the bill announced four weeks out with the headliner named and the
slot on the strip; the set as a door inside the invite (the hits /
the deep cut / the collab with the society friend on the same bill);
the night reusing `stageRead` plus a moment family; headlining a
tier-3 bill as a critical ceremony letter; regrets counted and read
back by the next organizer. The Japan weeks get the same card and
one in-country moment a week.

**3. The era, closed (every comeback's second half; SHIPPED v0.11.9, §100).** An `eraClosed`
family the week promotion ends — the last stage, the tally in words
(trophies, best chart week, the chodong's standing, the critics'
consensus), the room's state, the window if the drawer is stocked —
the ceremony the whole comeback lacks. The reissue as a scene
(`theReissue`: the A&R chair's pick as the bot's default, the fans'
pick, let it rest) with its MV tier and rounds shown instead of
inherited; announced through `eraAnnounced`'s family; the landing's
`eraExtended` reading the first act against the second; the
discography marking it. The pressing's pre-order week as a read and
the restock as a door. The debut's first stage named as a debut
stage.

**4. The long goodbye (SHIPPED in three: a member leaves, v0.11.10, §101; a group ends, v0.11.11, §102; across the street, v0.11.12, §103).** The farewell lap as an
object once the table sets `contract.leaving`, with three readers:
the release (a farewell-era mod and a note, hiatusReadsRelease's
shape), the last stage (critical, a family by voice), the member desk
(one door: tell the fans now or keep it in-house until the last era,
the fandom's temperature as the cost either way). The warm exit's
handwritten letter as a claim with a date and the bow read in reverse
like the finale — the eras, the center weeks, the trophies, the
friend she leaves, the chair she keeps. The disband as a scene with
doors (the last concert on the fancon machinery, the quiet statement,
the farewell record through the studio) and a final statement naming
what each member does next. `finalLineup` written on every ending;
an alumni strip so the open files are reachable; a departed idol who
can be signed across the street and a letter when she debuts there.

**5. The practice room, attended (the trainee years as episodes; part one, the mission, SHIPPED v0.11.13, §104; part two, the talk and the slot, SHIPPED v0.11.14, §105; part three, the year’s sheet, SHIPPED v0.11.16, §107; part four, the posting, SHIPPED v0.11.17, §108; the absences, part one, the return, SHIPPED v0.11.18, §109; part two, the wait, SHIPPED v0.11.19, §110; part three, the quiet, SHIPPED v0.11.20, §111).**
The evaluation sheet on a priority ladder (critical at a first #1,
the line or the talk; high within one of the line; flavor only when
nothing moved) naming the month's mission, her place and movement,
the line and one hash-picked moment that never repeats its kind
(the season's `lastMomentKind` shape); trajectory on the board from
`evalHistory`; a monthly theme the coaches announce so the two dials
have a reason to move; one door a month through the one queue (the
after-eval talk as a scene; the showcase slot as a pick); the
year-end sheet read in reverse as the loop's ceremony. The posting as
a critical letter for the room with a door for the ace left off. The
absences given a cadence from the fandom's side (the countdown
project, a letter from the base at the half, "whole again" as a
ceremony with the return stage named).

**6. The other side of the wall (rivals and the press as people; part one, the head, SHIPPED v0.11.22, §113; part two, the ledger, SHIPPED v0.11.23, §114; part three, the weight, SHIPPED v0.11.24, §115; part four, the letterhead, SHIPPED v0.11.25, §116; part five, the truce, SHIPPED v0.11.26, §117; the seat in play and the giants’ weeks measured and not built, §118).** A
hash-stamped HEAD per signing house (an invented name and a temper
word in the schools' pattern), shown on the card and quoted yearly in
the ranking letter through a family per temper. A directed ledger per
rival the way people have one (`tookOurWeek`, `lostHeadToHead`,
`signedTheirCastoff`, `declinedTheirJV`, `leveragedTheirOffer`,
`poachedFromUs`), read on the card in words and weighting what the
physics already roll (the ambush's target, intake interest, the JV
partner, the offer's suitor). One recurring door, `rivalCall`, opened
by temper (a borrowed stage week, a trainee swap, a joint gayo stage
with the society friend, a truce after a named rivalry), the polite no
as the bot's default. The overtake as a two-letter event ("the seat
is in play" in December, the ranking in January). The national
titans' mega-weeks on the strip through `announcedWeek` so they crowd
you and the date picker can see them; a torch letter when one
retires. The press given an outlet and a critic with memory — a
feature the player can sit for or refuse.

**7. The people upstairs and down the hall (the exec, the staff, the
company's file; part one, her own questions, SHIPPED v0.11.27,
§119; part two, the annual review, SHIPPED v0.11.28, §120; part
three, the company's own file, SHIPPED v0.11.29, §121; part four,
the written record, SHIPPED v0.11.30, §122; part five, the year's
close, SHIPPED v0.11.32, §124; part six, the label's birthday,
SHIPPED v0.11.36, §128; part seven, the greenlights on the record,
SHIPPED v0.11.37, §129; part eight, the handover, SHIPPED v0.11.39,
§131; part nine, the credits, SHIPPED v0.11.41, §133).** The
exec's `personality` finally read: a question
family per type (the profit hunter asks about the quarter, the
traditionalist about the vocal room, the micromanager about a trainee
by name from the eval board, the trend chaser about the sound of the
year); an annual review scene at board week in her voice with trust
bands that gate something visible — at "gone", probation with a dated
directive and the salaried door as the exit, which is the deferred
firing; a small exec-side ledger so the pitch she granted and the
greenlight honoured are remembered in words, and succession transfers
a record instead of a number. The staff given years: a yearly word
from each chair about her own room, credit on the eras she coached, a
tier-rise letter, leaving on her own terms, a market that remembers a
pass. The company's own file: a durable history written by the rails
that already fire (first debut, first trophy, first #1, the
breakthrough, settlements, foundings, successions, red episodes), a
"The company" page beside The record with the founding, the chapters
and the years under this manager (whose title finally changes), a
company anniversary on the founding week reusing the group
anniversary's family, and a year-end letter at week 48 from the
company to itself as the yearly accounting.

**8. The writing room talks back (the pitch and the commission as
meetings).** `thePitch` the week the demos land (take the sheet as it
is — the bot's lane; hear the pushed producer's second demo, priced;
send the wildcard back, his snub counter moving; ask for a rewrite
for the room); a `pitchMeeting` family and the demo-opinion strings
made families by salt. `theRewrite` on the commission's first-listen
moments (keep the brief / let them move / pull it); demo day as a
scene with the two seats' fogged lines (take it, shelve it to the era
drawer — feeding the reissue — or one more week). Writers as people:
heat words from the ledger that already exists, a `houseVoice`
narrative on the third record together, the writer's name in the
critics' quote when the lyric carried the record. The wardrobe
department from the shelf attaches here or to release 2: the stylist
chair, the choreographer chosen by name.

**Then the shelf, on the owner's call:** the imprint as the late-game
capstone (the founding machinery in reverse), the player-owned
academy, the offer's accept path.

**What this order leaves alone, on purpose.** The fandom (12) gains
its history page inside release 7 and its named nights inside
release 2 rather than a release of its own. The PR desk's missing
memory (a company that always apologises) is one ledger and a family,
a rider on release 6. The booking pile's towns with no promoter and
the financing's faceless funds are the same finding as the rivals'
missing heads — faces — and ride releases 6 and 7. No new market, no
new money instrument, no new system: everything above deepens a loop
a human already plays many times a career. The §39 honest
constraints stand — content is the budget (families × voices), and
the one queue is the ceiling on person-decisions until the owner
moves it.

**As built (v0.11.5 — the wiring).** Owner: *"Yeah start with the
wiring."* Recommendation 1 shipped whole, in four hands on one tree
(three slices by file ownership plus the door below), every number a
constant with its history comment, every new letter through the
rails and the trim, no rng draw added or removed inside a tick (the
two threshold changes — the festival invite and the promo offer —
keep their single draw and move only the bar), no top-level state
field added, every reader guarded so old saves load.

*The door.* graduateToSolo had no caller since v0.9.25 and the
return-run scene behind it was unreachable for anyone. The cold
renewal table now carries a third answer when she is a star
(`KP.graduateOpen`: rung 2+ or the word 'first among equals' or
above, a real lineup, the account covering the bonus): the solo
door — out of the lineup, in the family, a fresh seven on a solo
paper. It bills CONTRACT.graduateCost, deposits `openedTheDoor`,
lifts her and costs the room (graduateMorale 4 / graduateRoomMorale
2), writes the `graduatedSolo` letter and a feed family of three,
and the week her old group locks its next era, `returnRun` opens.
Never the bot's default; the ruling it leans on is §87 F read at the
table where she holds the cards — the company's last card is the
marquee, not the door. The soak band asserts the bot's silence.

*Render what exists.* Pure helpers, never a mint: `KP.gravityRead`
(the transcendence word on the dossier's Career tab, "In the room:",
and a chip on the member strip above the floor word),
`KP.renewalForecast` (the table's band on the contract line from
contract year five — a year before the folder — in the band's own
word), `KP.traineePaperRead` (the three-year paper and its notice
window on the dossier head and the roster row), `KP.tourRecordRead`
over a new `g.tourHistory` the wrap archives (TOUR.historyCap 8 —
"The road: N tours · last: club halls, 5 stops, 2 sold out"), the
booked festival slot on the calendar strip through KP.upcoming and
on the group page ("Booked: …", with the regrets clause), the Japan
ladder as a page (the partner, the rung in words, the next rung, the
JP fanbase as a band word), the books card reading the distributor's
tier, each club's tier and renewal, and the running quarter, the
company card reading the exec's tenure, the first trophy, the
chapters and the labels before this one, the rival card remembering
the offer either way, the road manager named with tenure in words,
the evaluation board and the roster chip carrying ▲/▼ and
climbing/parked/sliding from `p.evalHistory`. The power ranking's
score column is gone; "Since debut" reads in words (GROWTH_BANDS: a
step / a rung / a flight, up or down); the launch-solo modal says
what the engine does (she keeps her seat). A DOM stub joined the
test folder (`test/dom_stub.js`) so suites can pin rendered strings.

*The free answers, given their cost.* The offer: leverage and decline
are stamped on the house (`r.offerLeveraged` / `r.offerDeclined`)
and a leveraged house never sends a second envelope. The festival:
regrets and expiries are written on the group (`g.festRegrets`) and
next year's call for that festival comes through FESTS.
inviteAfterRegrets .45 instead of inviteChance .75 (the old literal,
now a constant), the invite and the body saying so. The distributor:
"stay" is remembered for DIST.recourtWeeks 52. Red ink: the expiry
costs each member BOOKS.redInkSilenceMorale and the room reads the
silence (`redInkSilence`). The clinic: the protective default still
benches her, and now writes the history line and `leftWaiting`
(`medLedger.restedBySilence`). The service: the plan's default costs
each man MIL.planSilenceMorale, the papers' default costs him
papersSilenceMorale and `leftWaiting`, both texts saying the room
noticed. Board season's third answer: every idol +1, trust −1, the
toast naming the trade. The interview's pass: remembered on the
hires ledger (cap HIRES.passMemoryCap 6) and twenty weeks later a
hash-picked house gives the candidate the chair in one normal letter
(`passedTookChair`). The promo desk: declines counted per desk, a
take clears them, two unanswered declines halve that desk's offer
chance on the same draw, the toast and the booking-desk lines
reading it. The lightstick: revenue sized by `KP.fanbaseRead` ×
CONSTITUENCY.lightstickPerFan .003 (break-even ~11.7k buyers; a
launch-week fandom leaves "boxes in the hallway", a flagship still
clears the run) — and the soak bot now waits until the fandom can
pay for it. The café notice reads: +1 intensity when it answers a
fresh grievance, −1 when it had nothing to say. The fandom's name:
the cafés' favorite (`KP.fandomFavoriteIdx`, the existing vote hash)
+2 when backed, −2 when overruled with the wanted name in the
letter, neutral when they decide. Unpairing writers and defusing a
rivalry write both files and the pair ledger; unpairing inside
PAIR.unpairSoonWeeks costs both a point. The met mandate: the exec
acknowledges a kept greenlight in a high letter (`mandateMet`) from
the mandates rail, the record itself the stash. The partner's "not
yet": each one (and each expiry) steps the next offer's cut by
JAPAN.notYetCutStep .03 to cutMax .34, the body and the letters
naming it in words, `KP.jpCut` reading the signed cut everywhere the
revenue splits. The new chair's two answers stay as they were, by
choice — a roleplay fork, not a free lunch.

*The record's moments.* The landing letter carries `ind: 'landed'`
at critical and the week's kept notes are stable-sorted so it leads;
its three lines point at the group's page, where the report button
has always lived. A debut's first stage is THE DEBUT STAGE (the
release archive's own `isDebut`), on the letter and the report chip.
The repackage's sentence is sent by the engine (`repackageSet`,
high) instead of discarded by the page, and the discography row
reads "extends “<title>”". The warehouse memo is back as a family of
three on the landing (`warehouseMemo`, high like the sold-out story
it mirrors — at normal it never survived a release week's dozen
letters, 0/40 in the first soak against 15/40 orgs that overpressed;
"nearly twice", "twice", "three times what the fandom bought";
PRODUCT.overpressDoubleAt 2 / overpressTripleAt 3), the release archives
demand / soldOut / overpress, and the report chip says
"overpressed". The restock door: a sold-out landing with
restockMinUnits (200) of demand still open after the late reorder
opens `restockCall` for restockFuseWeeks (2) — options[0] "let it
stay scarce" keeps every number the bot's soak had AND feeds the
fandom PRODUCT.scarceIntensity (2), the story the second run would
have sold; "press a second run" captures restockShare .6 of what is
left at the sheet's unit cost, the bill clamped to the account and
the units scaled to what was paid, the money through the chodong's
own path (margin, gifts, overseas, the distributor's cut, the
group's share), a high letter and `rel.restock`; the expiry is
silence and gets neither (the lead's ruling on the record agent's
note that the press dominated on money alone). The evaluation
sheet's priority ladder (EVAL.sheetHighMove 2): critical the month
the after-eval talk is held or the FIRST #1 in the building's
history is taken; high on a trainee's own first #1
(`flags.firstEvalTopWeek`, backfilled quietly on old files), a move
of two places either way, or the top changing hands; normal on a
smaller move; flavor only when nothing moved — one clause names the
story, and the talk's own letter is high. (The first cut made every
personal first #1 critical: seven criticals in ninety weeks of a
churning small room; the ruling above is the correction.) Season's
Greetings ship at normal. The reveal slips: the solo project's
spread reads without digits, and the solo drop, the unit era and the
OST line say "Reception: <word>". The allocation finally speaks:
`KP.allocLean` (DEBUT.allocLeanGap 15) names a vocal-heavy /
dance-heavy / camera-heavy room in the two-weeks-out countdown.

*The tools.* `test/dom_stub.js` — the audit's DOM stub, moved into
the test folder so a suite can pin rendered strings; suite_115
renders the dossier, the roster, the board, the group page, the
record and the company card and checks them for leaked tokens and
for state written at render (none). Fourteen measure-first counters
in the soak census for the new letters and stamps. The 0.11.5
migration only calls `KP.ensureLedgers` (the restock ledger exists
from week one).

*Measured (40 orgs, the second soak on the final code).* A passed
candidate's chair 36/40; the red-ink silence 0 (the bot answers every
scene); the kept greenlight 4; the warehouse memo 25 (15 whose last
release overpressed — at normal priority the letter reached 0, which
is how the §96 item 7 law was caught in its own release); the second
run 0 (bot never); the repackage announced 28; the landing critical
40; the sheet critical 40 and high 40; the solo door 0 (bot never);
the leveraged offer remembered 0 (the offer itself came to 16; the
bot leverages only when broke); regrets remembered 40; a desk cooled
0; the tour record 40; the lightstick 40 under the bot's new policy.
Bands ruled from these. Two owner-facing rulings worth their eye: the
restock door's default feeds the fandom (+2 intensity on every
answered sold-out call the bot takes — a small, deterministic move of
the soak's fandom numbers, kept because a free "scarce" would have
been the §96 agreement 4 bug reborn), and the evaluation sheet's
critical is reserved for the talk and the building's first #1.
Suite_115 (179) over test/dom_stub.js. Battery 115/115, soak 40
clean (twice), longhaul 11 × 620 clean, e2e 134, lockstep 0.11.5.
Migration 0.11.5 (ensureLedgers).

## §97 The offers tab (SHIPPED v0.11.6)

Owner, with a screenshot of a Desk whose rail held four booking cards
and nothing else above the fold: *"This, here with all of the offers,
it's taking up the whole feed on the desk. I want an offers tab where
all of the stages, endorsement opportunities, etc goes and shows a
number each week for the number of offers to check."*

**The ruling.** The one desk (§89 D15) put every answer owed on one
rail — decisions first, then the market's asks. The pile (§76 D)
deals faster than a small label can read, so the asks buried the
decisions. The line drawn: a DECISION is a person at the door or a
table with the company's name on it — the renewal, the diagnosis, the
term sheet, the courting call, the partner's letter, the last
statement; an OFFER is something the market asks the label to take or
pass — a stage from the pile, a brand or a second job, a festival
bill, a broadcaster's invitation, a brand that wants the face alone.
Decisions stay on Today. Offers move to their own tab with the count
on it, and Today says in one line how many wait.

**As built.** `KP.offersRead(state)` (sim.js) — pure, never writes:
the open bookings, the open outside offers and the scenes of
`KP.offerSceneKinds` (festivalInvite, promoOffer, sponsorSolo), each
list sorted by answer-by, soonest first, each stage and call a COPY
marked `fresh` when it arrived this week (bookings: expiresWeek −
BOOK.expireWeeks; calls: expiresWeek − OUTSIDE.expiresWeeks; scenes:
their own week), with `count` and `fresh`. The Desk's sub-tab row
reads Today · Offers · Building · Content · Record, the Offers button
wearing a magenta badge with the count. Today's rail renders only the
decision scenes through the one scene card and, where the pile used to
be, one gold line — "N offers on the table — M new this week — the
Offers tab." — that switches the tab. The tab leads with the count and
then three kickers with theirs: Stages (the pile's cards with Send and
+ flyer week, and a line when nobody in the building can take a
stage), Bills and broadcasters (the scene cards), Endorsements and
second jobs (Sign it / Book it / Pass); fresh asks wear a "new" chip;
an empty tab says so. Every button is the one the rail carried, so no
handler moved. The e2e's outside-offer walk taps the tab first.
Suite_116 (22) over the DOM stub, including the law that a render
writes nothing. No engine behaviour changed; the soak is unmoved.

## §98 The stages, lived (SHIPPED v0.11.7 — §96 recommendation 2)

Owner: *"Go ahead with release 2."* The §96 survey graded the tour a
10 and festival season a 9: the road is the televised season's
nearest cousin — a plan, silent weeks of near-identical letters, a
one-line count — and the engine already rated every night without
one of them reaching a door, a card or the calendar; a festival was
one invite body, one sentence per night, and declining was free
(the wiring priced the regrets). This release gives both the
season's shape on the same mechanisms: a card you read every week,
a letter that names a moment, doors during the run, and a ceremony
at the end. Who sells out, who runs soft and what a night is worth
did not move; every default is today's behaviour, every new number
is hashed, and the soak forks byte-identical for an unchanged choice.

**The plan.**

*The road.* (1) Every night on the record: `tour.dates[]` keeps the
city or region, the week, the band and whether it sold out, ran
soft or earned the encore. (2) "On the road" on Today, like "On the
air": the scale and leg, the next stop named before it plays, the
room against demand in words, last night's band, the sold-outs and
encores so far, the last night of the tour on the calendar strip.
(3) Three doors during the road, none of them the bot's: the ENCORE
NIGHT (the second night the promoter booked — play it, or hand it
back so the room sleeps: the fee goes back, the fatigue comes off);
the ROAD PRESSER after a fumbled night (ride it — the next room
sells a shade softer, today's law — or put out a statement that
costs a little money and a little hype and steadies the next room);
the SETLIST SWAP when the fandom's b-side pick is loud (keep the
hits, or sing the pick — the fandom pays in intensity). (4) A
moment family on every leg letter, never the same kind two weeks
running: the crowd sang her lines, the ment that went long, the
sign in two languages, the rain set, the first-timer's sign, the
hometown stop, the encore chant, the curtained upper tier, the van
asleep. The leg letter rides at high. (5) The wrap as a ceremony: a
critical letter reading the route date by date, the night that went
wrong and the one that went right named, the encores and the
moments counted — and the tour record on the group page keeps the
best and worst night.

*Festival season.* (6) The bill, posted when the organizers call
four weeks out: the edition's lineup cast from the rival acts by
popularity, the headliner named, our act on it once booked; the
invite body reads the bill, and an Industry card lists the season's
upcoming bills with our status. (7) The set as a door inside the
invite: take the slot with the hits (the default), the deep cut the
fandom asked for, or the collab with the society friend's act on the
same bill — or regrets. (8) The night as a moment: the play letter
names a hash-picked moment (the golden-hour fancam, the rain set,
the b-side singalong, the ment that went long, the wrong banner, the
lightstick ocean, the collab) and who played before and after us.
(9) Headlining a top-tier bill is a critical ceremony letter reading
the poster top to bottom with our slot last.

*Japan.* (10) The in-country weeks stop being silent: one letter a
week from a moment family (the billboard, the radio spot in slow
Japanese, the fan letter in katakana, the soundcheck, the
convenience-store photo), and an "In Japan" card on Today beside the
road card.

*The census.* tourLedger (encores offered / handed back, pressers
offered / statements, swaps offered / taken, moments, ceremonies),
festivalLedger (bills posted, deep sets, collabs, ceremonies,
moments), jpLedger (away moments); bands measure-first, the bot
learning the new doors with a cautious hand (hand back the encore at
a worn room, a statement when flush, the swap and the deep set when
the fandom is loud, the collab when a friend is on the bill).

**As built (v0.11.7).** Everything above shipped, in two hands on one
tree (the road; festival season and Japan), the bot's path
byte-identical to v0.11.6 on every default — the tour half proved it
against the pre-release engine week by week — every new number a
TOUR or FESTS constant with its history, no rng draw added or
removed inside a tick, the new randomness hashed.

*The road.* `tour.dates[]` keeps every night (the city or region,
the week, the band, sold out / soft / the earned encore, the week's
moment). `KP.tourRoadRead` is the pure read behind "On the road ·
<group>" on Today — the scale and leg, the next stop named before it
plays, the room in words (a room they will fill twice / a full room
/ a warm room / a room with curtains ready), last night's band, the
sold-outs and second nights, the home date — and behind the Studio
hero's "Next:" line and the strip's "last night of the tour". Three
doors open inside the tour's week with a one-week fuse, one at a
time, never on the tour's last week: ENCORE NIGHT the week a city
earns the second night (the encore is still booked and paid in the
tick; play it, or hand it back — the deposit returns, clamped, the
counts step down, every present member rests TOUR.encoreRestFatigue
6, a letter says the room slept); ROAD PRESSER after a fumbled night,
once per leg (ride it — the next room sells at the stage's bad-night
law — or a statement for presserCost 4 and presserHype 1 that steadies
the next room: `KP.nightDemandMult` returns 1 once while
`tour.pressered`); SETLIST SWAP on the first week of a hits tour when
the latest record's fan pick is loud (swapPickHeat 62 or the sleeper):
keep the hits, or sing the pick for swapIntensity 3 and the singalong
moment. `KP.tourMomentOf` picks one of ten kinds a week by hash, never
the same kind twice running (she sang the lines, the ment went long,
the sign in two languages, the rain set at rainChance .25, the
first-timer, the hometown stop from `born.city`, the encore chant,
the curtained upper tier, the van asleep, the singalong), two or three
lines each, appended to both leg letters, which now ride at high. The
wrap is critical and reads the route date by date, names the night
that went right and the one that went wrong, counts the encores and
the moments; the tour record on the group page keeps best and worst.
`state.tourLedger` (encores offered / handed back, pressers offered /
statements, swaps offered / taken, moments, ceremonies), in
ensureLedgers.

*Festival season.* The bill is composed once per edition the week
the organizers call (`state.festBills`, in ensureLedgers): the rival
acts that are live and clear the bar, by popularity with a hash
tie-break, FESTS.billSize 6, the headliner named; `KP.festivalBillRead`,
`KP.festivalPoster` (our act spliced by popularity, or on top when we
headline) and `KP.festivalSeasonRead` (the next seasonCardCount 3
editions with our status) are pure. The invite body reads the bill;
the Industry tab's "Festival season" card lists the editions with the
headliner, three poster names (ours in gold) and our status in words.
The invite's options read accept · deep · collab · decline: the deep
cut when the latest record's hottest b-side is warm (deepPickHeat
58), the collab when a society friend's act is on this bill; both book
exactly like accept and store the set on the booking. The night names
its neighbours ("on after X, before Y") and a hash-picked moment from
seven kinds (golden hour on a tier-2 bill, the rain set at .2, the
singalong on a deep set, the ment that went long, the wrong banner at
.15, the lightstick ocean at intensity 55, the collab), never the same
kind twice; the deep set feeds the fandom deepIntensity 2; the collab
is remembered on the friendship and, at collabViralChance .35 by hash,
spikes the leader's following and writes the clip's letter. A tier-3
headline is one critical ceremony letter reading the poster bottom to
top with our act last, the band word, the moment and the fee.
festivalLedger gains billsPosted, deepSets, collabs, ceremonies,
moments.

*Japan.* Every in-country week after the landing writes one normal
letter — "In Japan, week N of M" — from six kinds by hash (the
billboard on an invented crossing, the radio spot in slow Japanese
with the voice abroad or the interpreter, the fan letter in katakana,
the soundcheck in the hall the rung booked, the convenience-store
photo, the train platform), never the same kind twice; `g.jpAway`
keeps the week's moment, `KP.japanAwayRead` is the pure read behind
"In Japan · <group>" on Today beside the road card; jpLedger.awayMoments.

*The hand the bot learned.* Hand the second night back when the room
averages 75 fatigue, a statement when the account holds 300, the pick
and the deep cut when the fandom's intensity is 50, the collab whenever
a friend is on the bill; otherwise the house default.

*A finding for the next release.* Both agents found, independently,
that `KP.hashStr` (FNV-1a without a final mix) barely moves when only
the tail of a key changes: a key ending in the week gives near-constant
values week after week (0.41 … 0.44 across eight consecutive weeks in
the lead's own probe, against a full spread when the week leads). The
kernel's `KP.lineFor` keys `[seed, salt, week]` with the week LAST, so
a family keyed by one salt tends to pick the same line every week
unless a caller passes its own memory — part of the repetition the
owner reported in §93 survived the expansion for that reason. This
release keyed its own picks safely (the week mid-key, or the key
pre-hashed) and left the kernel alone, because fixing hash01 moves
every hash read — including the season's judged weeks — and belongs in
its own measured release (§99).

*Measured (40 orgs).* The encore door offered 40/40, handed back 0
(the bot's worn-room bar is rarely met on humane pacing; suite-held);
the road presser 1, the statement 1; the setlist swap offered 24,
sung 20; a moment on the leg letters 40; the wrap as a ceremony 40;
the road card 40; bills posted 40; the deep cut 17; the collab 38
(friends form in promo weeks and the bot collabs whenever one is on
the bill); a festival moment 40; the tier-3 headline ceremony 0
(icons plus the bar inside 140 weeks is rare; suite-held); Japan's
weeks 40. Bands ruled from these. One older band re-pointed: the
lottery ticket's org count read 37/40 against its .90 ceiling while
the rate the census prints fell 0.74 → 0.63 revivals per org-year —
fewer revivals, spread wider by the stages' small intensity moves;
the rate is the flood guard, the ceiling moves to .97 with the
history on it. Suite_117 (134) folded from the two slices'
verification scripts, the DOM stub rendering the Industry card.
Battery 117/117, soak 40 clean, longhaul 11 × 620 clean, e2e 135,
lockstep 0.11.7. Migration 0.11.7 (ensureLedgers: tourLedger,
festBills).

## §99 The hash (SHIPPED v0.11.8 — a kernel law, found by two hands at once)

**The finding.** Building §98, the tour slice and the festival slice
reported the same thing within an hour of each other: `KP.hash01`
barely moved when the only varying part of a key sat at its END.
`KP.hashStr` is FNV-1a — xor the byte, multiply by the prime, byte
by byte — with no final mix, so the last characters of a key reach
only the low bits of the word, and `hash01` divides the whole word by
2³², which is to say it reads the HIGH bits. A key shaped
`seed|salt|week` therefore gave 0.41, 0.42, 0.41, 0.42, 0.44, 0.44,
0.43, 0.43 across eight consecutive weeks in the lead's own probe,
while the same parts with the week first gave 0.91, 1.00, 0.94, 0.86,
0.89, 0.95, 0.17, 0.47. The kernel's `KP.lineFor` keys
`[seed, salt, week]` — week last. Every flavor family keyed by one
salt was picking the same line week after week unless its caller
carried a memory (the spotlight's `spotMem`, the season's
`lastMomentKind`); the §93 expansion's census counted repeats across
an org-year and could not see a family stuck on one line for one
salt. The same shape sat under mechanics: the season's weekly noise
(`[seed, contestant, tag, week]`), so a contestant's ranking noise
stood still from week to week; the mother-fund's yearly window
(`[seed, 'motherfund', year]`), so a career's window was open every
year or closed every year; the chart rotation jitter per act per
week; the fan pick's flip; the Monday question's branch; the show
desk an offer came from; the fund letterhead a pitch drew; the
regular's handle; the titans' pulse; the knock queue's tie-break;
the weekly social-growth noise per person, a fixed bias per file.

**The law.** `KP.hash01` applies a final avalanche (murmur3's fmix32)
to the FNV word before dividing. A key's parts may sit in any order.
`KP.hashStr` is untouched — the rng seeds derive from it and the
world's rng streams do not move. `KP.hash01Legacy` keeps the old
value for the one migration that needs it.

**What a hash change touches.** Everything hashed changes value at
the version boundary. Almost everything hashed is either stamped
into state at its birth (the schools' tempers, the pre-known flags,
the season's show and cast, the bills, the fandom's name once
chosen) or is flavor that may change its mind (which line, which
moment, which word). The one hidden TRUTH derived from the hash at
read time was the staff's aptitude (`KP.staffTruth`: the base, the
gem, the best seat, off the seat's id) — under a new hash every
chair in every save would have re-rolled. So the truth is minted
once now: `truthFor` stamps `st.truth` at the interview, at the
founding, and — by the 0.11.8 migration, with the legacy hash — on
every chair and every waiting candidate in an existing save, and
`KP.staffTruth` reads the file (the derivation remains the fallback
for a chair no migration touched; it never writes). An existing
save will see three honest one-time moves on load: the chart's
rotation jitter re-rolls this week, a season in progress re-rolls
its remaining weekly noise and edit timing, and the mother-fund
window may read differently from the January letter for the rest of
the year. None of them is a stored fact contradicted; all are the
hash finally doing what it was for.

**What the fixtures taught.** Twenty-two assertions in seventeen
suites broke under the new hash — seventeen as failures, five as
crashes on a `find` that came back empty — and not one of them was
the hash's fault: every one had been pinned to the line, the offset or
the gate the stuck hash happened to give its seed. The bench letter is a four-line family and the test matched
the first line's words — and the clinic's door, added since, writes
"Pulled from the schedule for" on the same file where the schedule
bench writes "by medical staff", so the seed search had stopped at the
wrong door. The birthday family's third line says "is N now", not
"turns N". The sleeper fixture set the chance to 1 and the cap priced
the roll at .60 — luck, not law. The catalog push's "never paid out"
forgot that a resurfaced clip prices the roll on its own. The board's
age-out fixture rode a year on no income, the label folded, and a
dissolved company's tick is a no-op until the chapter is answered —
the assertion was reading a board that had stopped moving. A stage
fixture's sheet changed under it, because the sheet's shares and the
song's demand are the record's own and the load law makes a bigger
share a harder bar (the moment fixtures pin an even sheet now; the
load law keeps its own block). A trainee hit the wall in the same tick
her promise expired, and the letter waited for her to be back in the
room. A storm handed the solo-launch fixture a hiatus. A first-advance
eval left a bottom streak that made the next sheet's talk critical. A
cut rival trainee came back through the released door because the
board was full. The spotlight's rota starts at a weekly hash, and the
sting fixture rode four weeks at the one offset the first hash gave
its seed; the bubble's 7% weekly gate had been held open for the scar
fixture's idol every week; the quiet-week family has three lines and
the test matched one; the anniversary letter is high, and a loud week
outranks high. And one that was not a fixture's fault: an eliminated
contestant from the open board went home and was forgotten, because
the known-file test (`KP.hasChapter`) read the desk's flags and never
the television — a televised run is public knowledge now, and the
season's cast is kept as "gone", never deleted. Two readings are law: a test reads the week's wire
pre-trim (`KP.lastTickNotes`), and a fixture forces the mechanism it
claims — every gate of it — never a roll it happens to win.

**What the census found.** Three things the soak could only say once
the hash moved. (1) Twenty of forty orgs "pulled out" of festival
slots, every one from Japan. The lane has refused to fly over a
booking since the v0.11.3 audit, but an open invitation is not yet a
booking — the act flew, then the desk said yes to a slot inside the
trip. The signing reads the calendar now: `KP.festivalHardClash`
(Japan to the lane's end, the road to the booking desk's estimate of
its weeks, an official hiatus) refuses accept, deep cut and collab
with the reason, and the invitation stays open to lapse or to regret;
`KP.planTour` gained the lane's guard (a booking inside the planned
span refuses the road); the miss's cause is ledgered
(`festivalLedger.missedWhy`) and the census prints it; the bot sends
regrets on a clash. Measured after: 0/40 pulled out (the band stays
0–50%: a hiatus announced over a booking is still a miss, and still
costs the room). (2) The passed-over ace fell from 8–10/40 to 5/40:
the perceived read's key ended in the domain and the observation
count, so under the old hash a person's five talents carried one
error that never shrank with watching, and the sheet's #1 disagreed
with the lineup more often than the fog deserved. The band's floor
moves to .05 with the history on it — a story, not a rate. (3) A
rival merger moved its trainees between letterheads without a line on
their files ("Signed to Lantern" … "Cut at Dawnhak's evaluation"):
the file says what happened now (§90 D).

*Measured.* The repeat census counts a template's repeats across an
org-year and moved only within noise (notes top 2.3 → 2.1 per
org-year, feed 6.8 → 7.0, spotlight 3.4 → 3.6): it never could see a
family stuck on one line for one salt, which is what suite_118 pins
directly — a three-line family uses all three lines inside twelve
weeks; the mother-fund window opens some years and closes others; ten
consecutive tail-varying keys spread more than .5 where the legacy
hash drifted less than .1. Suite_118 (20). Battery 118/118, soak 40
clean, longhaul 11 × 620 clean, e2e 134 (one conditional
branch fewer than 0.11.7's 135), lockstep 0.11.8. Migration 0.11.8
(ensureLedgers; `st.truth` stamped on every chair and every waiting
candidate with the legacy hash).

## §100 The era, closed (SHIPPED v0.11.9 — §96 recommendation 3)

Owner: *"Approved to tackle as much of the remaining queue as you see
fit."* The queue's third entry. The §96 survey found that every
comeback had a first half (the announcement, the teasers, the landing,
the comeback stage) and then promotion simply ran out: no letter said
the era was over, the trophies and the last stage were never read
back, and the reissue was a panel in the Studio that inherited its
video and its rounds from whatever the last lock form happened to
hold. This release is the second half. One new module, `era.js`, and
it makes no draw anywhere: every pick in it is a hash.

**The close.** The week after the last promotion week
(`state.week === g.promoUntil + 1`, exact equality; weekly order 596,
after the week's stages at 580 and promotion at 585, before a landing
at 600) the desk reads the era back in one high letter, `eraClosed`.
Four verdicts (`KP.eraVerdict`): CROWNED when the era's own shelf
holds a trophy, which outranks the reception's word; WARM for a
record that landed strong or a sensation; COLD for a miss; QUIET for
the rest. Each verdict is a family of three opening lines through
`KP.lineFor`, never the same line twice running (`g.lastCloseLine`).
Then the last stage in words (carried, and by whom; clean; wobbled;
fumbled; or "the era ended off the schedule" when no broadcaster had
the group in its last week). Then the tally in words: the trophies;
the best chart week, with the national board in brackets; the first
week in copies, with "a career best", "the pressing sold through" or
"boxes left in the warehouse"; and the critics, who either "settled
on" a word or are "still arguing, the middle voice at" one. A split
verdict was told its arguments would outlast the promotion, and the
close does not say the critics settled when they did not. Then the
second wind, if the era took one; the room in a word (fresh, tired,
spent: the average fatigue of the members present against 45 and 70,
never a digit); and, when the drawer is stocked, the window and "the
call is on the desk".

It claims something: a crowned close lifts the morale of every member
present by 3 and a cold one costs 2 (`ERA.closeMoraleUp`,
`closeMoraleDown`). It leaves a mark: `rel.closed = { week, trophies,
lastStage, verdict, room }` (and `extended`), which the discography
on the group page reads ("closed with 2 trophies", "closed warm after
a second wind", "reissued as …", "left to rest"). Two facts had to
start being kept for the close to have anything to read: `rel.trophies`
(shows.js, counted beside the group's own shelf) and `rel.lastStage`
(the week's notable stage, overwritten each promotion week, so an
extension's stage is the true last one).

**The reissue is a door.** A close with a stocked drawer opens
`theReissue` on the Desk, on the ground `KP.planRepackage` already
stood on (`KP.reissueOpenFor`: not a single, not itself a reissue,
not rested, no lock in flight, nobody in Japan, on the road or in a
solo era). The picks are stamped when the door opens. The A&R chair
hears the strongest hook left in the drawer. The fan desk reads the
cafés, who want more of the era's own sound and, among that, whatever
will look best on a stage; with none of the era's sound left, the
best stage in the whole drawer (`sc.fansWhy`). Three answers: the
chair's pick, which is the bot's default; the fans' pick, when it
differs; or let the era rest. Each reissue answer carries the video
tier, the fan-sign rounds and the bill on its label. Resting is a
real answer: the record is marked `reissueRested`, the drawer closes
for good, and every member present gets 8 fatigue back
(`ERA.restRelief`). The fans' pick, or a pick both desks agree on,
warms the fandom by 2. Silence is the worst answer: the door lapses
with the window, six weeks after promotion, with no reissue and no
rest handed back. A new lock supersedes the door. Every outcome is
counted on `state.eraLedger` (closed, reissueOffered, anr, fans,
desk, rested, lapsed, superseded).

The Studio keeps its panel, and the panel is now the reissue's own
sheet: the video tier and the rounds are chosen there (the desk's
build by default, `KP.reissueBuild`: a standard video and the
suggested rounds), the drawer marks whose pick is whose, and the
panel says the same call is waiting on the Desk. One bill is quoted
everywhere (`KP.reissueBill`: the record at the reprint's 55%, the
video at the group's stature, the pressing, the home discount), and
it is the real bill. Before, a reissue paid for no pressing at all
and then settled against a full-size sheet it never chose, so it
overpressed by construction; the soak's bot met the warehouse memo
almost nowhere else. The pressing is now sized to the reprint's
share of demand (`KP.reissuePressing`: 55% of the run and of the
lock read) and billed, and the cost accrues to the group's ledger
and to the era's spend.

The announcement goes out through `eraAnnounced`'s family, marked
`reissue`, public and high; the old `repackageSet` ind is retired.
It says what the reissue is made of ("with a standard MV and no
fan-sign rounds on the sheet. It lands …"). The landing's
`eraExtended` letter reads the second act against the first: the two
reception words ("The first act landed quiet; the second lands
solid, which is the rarer direction for a reprint to travel."), then
the two chart peaks ("It opens at #3, under the first act's #1.").
The lock carries the first act's word and peak for that
(`prep.repackage.band`, `.chartPeak`), and the first act's file is
marked `reissuedAs`. The reissue's own close ends "That closes both
acts: “…” landed quiet, and its reissue solid." and opens no second
door: an era extends once.

**One era, two acts (the red ledger).** Because the reissue now
carries a bill, its net joins the first act's instead of standing as
a second era (debut.js, the landing). `g.lastEraNet` becomes the sum.
A red era that the reissue brings level clears the count and reopens
the hard conversation (zero is black). A level era that the reissue
tips under is counted, once. The same era is never counted twice.
Before, the reissue had no bill on the era and stood as an era of its
own, so any reissue wiped the red count, and one that lost money
would have counted the same era a second time.

**The pre-order week, as a read.** One week before the shelf (order
591, behind the T-1 teaser) the distributor's count arrives as a
normal letter, `preorderWeek`: the count against the pressing, and a
word. The read is the settle's own sum. `KP.demandRead` is the
settle's arithmetic up to the reception, lifted out of
`KP.settleProduct` so the pre-order week reads the same number the
landing will finish; the settle multiplies it by the reception, the
noise and the reissue's share in the old order, so every first-week
number lands on the unit it always did. The word is the settle's
verdict on an ordinary week, a middling record with no luck either
way: AHEAD when that week sells the run out, SOFT when it leaves the
warehouse memo (`PRODUCT.overpressAt`, 1.6), TRACKING between. It
has no thresholds of its own, on purpose. The first build carried
two, against a different sum (`KP.preorderRead`'s campaign factor,
which the settle never reads), and the soak measured the word as
wallpaper: 569 of 665 landings read ahead and none soft. The word is
stamped on the lock (`prep.preorder`), archived on the record
(`rel.pressing.preorder`), and the close says how it held up: "the
pre-order week called it", "read it wrong", "the record outran its
pre-orders", "fell short of its pre-orders". A reissue's pressing
gets a read of its own, at the reprint's share. The record also
keeps which sheet the run was (`rel.pressing.preset`).

**The second wind belongs to its promotion.** `g.eraExtendedWeek`
was written at the extension and never cleared, so one extension
shut the door for the rest of a career, and every later promotion
wore "· extended" in the Studio. `KP.eraExtended(g)` reads the stamp
against the last landing: older than that, it is another era's.
Read, not cleared, so an old save carries its stale stamp and needs
no migration.

**The closed broadcast door.** Found while pinning the lock.
`KP.planDebut` swapped a plan's show slots to radio (the door closed
to a label nobody has heard of, §76) in the caller's own plan,
before the till could refuse the lock. A refused lock retried with
the same plan found no show left to swap and told nothing, and the
day the shows opened was no news to a label that had never been told
they were closed. The lock works on its own copy now, and the letter
goes out from the lock that happens.

**Old saves.** Migration 0.11.9 (ensureLedgers). An era already past
its last promotion week is never closed after the fact: the close
fires on the exact week. An era the file is in the middle of is not
closed either, because before this build no record kept its
trophies or its last stage, and that close would say "no trophy"
over a shelf that holds two. `KP.migrate` knows a file from before
the era module by the ledger's absence, read before the chain runs,
and stamps the week the file learned to keep the record
(`eraLedger.since`); the close passes over any record that landed
before it. A record that lands the week of the stamp has every
promotion week ahead of it and closes whole. A new game carries no
such week. A reissue the old build had already locked lands on the
terms it was signed on: no pressing sheet (the settle sizes one as
it always did, and may overpress as it always did), no pre-order
read, no comparison it was never given a word for. Its close still
reads both acts, because the first act's landing word was always on
file.

**The timeline.** `eraClosed` echoes on the feed, two lines in two
voices for each verdict; the reissue's announcement has three lines
of its own. Both are picked by hash and draw nothing, so the feed's
stream stands where it stood. The lock's letter is a desk letter
(`fed: false`), read by the next week's feed pass.

**The Desk's cards.** Seen in a real browser, not in the stub: the
door's three answers, each a title, a build and a bill, stood as
three columns 110px wide and ten lines tall on a phone.
`UI.answersStack`: an answer that would run past three lines in its
share of the row takes a row of its own (two answers share a row up
to forty characters, three up to twenty-four, four up to twelve).
Every decision card draws through the one component, so the rule
reaches all of them: of the 45 scene kinds that opened across eight
seeds, 12 always stack, 4 sometimes, 29 never.

**The bot.** It answers the door: it rests an era under fiscal
pressure or one that landed under 62; otherwise it wants the bill
covered half again before it signs; it takes the fans' pick only
for a cold fandom (intensity under 45); it may leave the door open
while the account is short, and the door may lapse. It no longer
reaches for the reissue unprompted. It signs the second wind through
the staff's flag while the room is under 75, the line the encore
already uses. A probe over 40 seeds had found 657 last promotion
weeks, 95 of them with a record still climbing, and 92 of those
flagged tired: the boss that signed only an unflagged room took 3
doors in twelve years, and the census row measured its caution
instead of the verb. And it learned the pressing ladder (cautious,
the desk's sheet, bold): up a rung after a sellout, down after a
memo, lean only after two red quarters running.

*Measured (40 orgs; the era rows also at 120 seeds before they were
ruled).* A close read 40; the door offered 40; the chair's pick 32;
the fans' pick 4; a Studio build 0 (the bot never); rested 40;
lapsed 1; superseded 0; the pre-order read 40, ahead 38, soft 39;
the second wind offered 36, signed through the flag 7, a closed era
marked extended 10; an era extended on a climbing record 10 (the row
had read 3 to 8 under the cautious boss). Three older bands moved,
with the history on them: the sold-out row keeps its band at 31/40
and has its label corrected (it samples each group's last landing,
never the archive); the warehouse floor .20 → .05 (7/40: the memo
now belongs to the bold run after a sellout, because the suggested
sheet almost never overpresses and the reissue no longer does by
construction); the mash's acclaim ceiling .60 → .75 (the row follows
`fusionTried` and cannot sit under it; nothing here touches the
mash's roll). The final soak is byte-identical to the one before the
old-file rule went in: that rule moves nothing in a new game.

*Known limits.* The desk's letters queue behind the whole week's
wire, so a loud week can crowd a desk letter's echo out of the
eight-post week; what is promised, and pinned, is that the week's
own pass reads the letter and clears the mark. No migration sizes a
pressing sheet for a reissue the old build locked.

*Already shipped.* Two of recommendation 3's lines went out early, in
the wiring (v0.11.5): the restock as a door (`restockCall`) and the
debut's first stage named as a debut stage.
